subject: Edge finishing and assembly quality
hook: 0.4, 1 or 2 mm? Match the edge to the job.
ig:
0.4, 1 or 2 mm? Choosing the right ABS edge for each panel saves money where it doesn't show and adds strength where it does.

A quick guide for kitchen fitters, joiners and anyone sending us a cutting list:

0.4 mm: hidden edges. Shelf backs, carcass edges against walls.
1 mm: general carcass work. Visible but not in the firing line.
2 mm: doors, drawer fronts and high-wear edges that get knocked.

Two things that matter as much as thickness:

Colour match. Put the board décor on the list so the edge matches the face.
Edge marking. Show which edges are banded and in what thickness on every line. It's the single biggest cause of questions on incoming lists.

We band 0.4, 1 and 2 mm ABS in our Hanley workshop, alongside cutting, drilling and assembly.

Save this for your next job, and send your cutting list via the link in bio for a priced quote.
fb:
For the trade: a quick guide to choosing ABS edge thickness, because it's one of the most common questions on cutting lists we receive.

Hidden edges like shelf backs can take 0.4 mm. Visible carcass edges generally suit 1 mm. Door and drawer fronts and anything that gets knocked are better in 2 mm. And whatever the thickness, name the board décor so the edge matches the face.

Most importantly, mark every edge on your list. It saves calls and keeps your job moving through the workshop.

We offer panel cutting, edging, drilling and assembly from our Hanley workshop. Send us your cutting list for a priced quote.
